model: H-Max HVAC drive (embedded Modbus RTU / TCP)
applies_to: H-Max HVAC drives with the application described in application manual MN04008006E (January 2012).
summary: The Eaton H-Max is an HVAC variable frequency drive with built-in RS-485 (Modbus RTU, N2, BACnet MS/TP) and Ethernet (Modbus TCP, BACnet IP). Its Modbus map uses fixed process-data blocks for control and status plus direct access to application IDs. This map covers the control/status words, speed reference, the default process-data outputs, coils/discrete inputs and the RTU settings.

addressing.note: The manual says data addresses start at zero (holding register 40001 = address 0) and prints the map 1-based; its write example sends start address 07D0h (2000) for control word 2001 and its read example sends 0836h (2102) for register 2103. Subtract 1 from every printed number; application ID n is register n, wire n-1. Coils 0001-0003 are 1-based too (coil 1 = wire 0); discrete inputs printed 10001-10008 are Modicon-style references for wire 0-7.

source.title: H-Max HVAC Drives Application Manual
source.pages: monitoring IDs p. 18; RS-485 protocol p. 57; Modbus RTU/TCP parameters pp. 98-103; data mapping pp. 103-107; example frames pp. 108-109; process data out table p. 114

notes: This copy is hosted by the US distributor Precision Electric; it is Eaton manual MN04008006E (January 2012).
The 32-bit status word is printed as 2151 = high data, 2152 = low data, so it is high word first (ABCD). The 16-bit control/status words at 2001/2101 carry only the lower 16 bits.

Process data out 1-8 scales come from the annex table (output frequency 0.01 Hz, speed 1 rpm, current 0.1 A, torque/power 0.1 %, voltage 0.1 V, DC link 1 V); the manual's read example decodes 09C4h at 2104 as 25.00 Hz. They are typed UINT16 here; signedness is not stated.
Registers 2002 and 2102 are reserved. Process data in 1-8 are application-defined and carry no fixed meaning.
All holding registers can also be read with function 04 at the same address.

Left out: monitoring IDs other than 37, because the H-Max monitoring table lists IDs and units but no scale; the operation-day, energy and fault-history counters at 40001-40430, which the manual prints as both 40001 and 440001, so their wire address is ambiguous; the ID map ranges (usable, but empty until configured).

integration.summary: Select Fieldbus as the remote control place, then write the control word to 2000 and the speed reference (0-10000 = 0-100 %) to 2002 in one write. Read status 2100 and process data out 2103-2110 for frequency, current and fault code.
integration.enable: Select Modbus RTU as the RS-485 protocol (P4.7.1.1, ID 2208), set slave address, baud and parity under I/O and Hardware > RS-485, then set the remote control place to Fieldbus control (Basic Parameters > Start Src Auto) and the auto speed reference to fieldbus.
integration.watchdog: P4.7.3.1.4 RTU communication time-out (default 10 s, 0 = not used) and P4.8.2.1.3 for Modbus TCP raise a fieldbus fault when polling stops.
quirks: The 32-bit control/status words are high word first; the 16-bit copies hold only bits 0-15.
setup: RTU defaults: address 1, 9600 baud, no parity with 2 stop bits.
Terminate both ends of the RS-485 line; the manual recommends active biasing for idle-bus stability.
gotchas: The drive ignores fieldbus run commands unless Fieldbus is the active control place (status word bits 29-31).
